analysis:
The only change is a documentation edit in docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md (head lines ~676-684). It describes how `darkbloom cluster stop`, `darkbloom stop` and `restart` end the cluster setup wait, and how the joining Mac learns of a stop. The leading Mac counts each stop request and its status carries the count. A bare "Stopped" status is no longer treated as a stop, replacing the 0.10.9-0.10.12 behavior of inferring one after 20 seconds. I reviewed both base text units (lines 472-1306). The base text has no source or config changes.

I found no security regression. No code, permission, key, attestation, or coordinator contract changes here. The edit narrows an availability and false-stop behavior: the join screen no longer aborts on a transient "Stopped" status during a download or copy. That touches A-018 serving availability only as documentation, and the threat model's provider-control boundaries are not changed.

Open integration questions: the described stop-count mechanism (a stop counter carried in the leading Mac's status, read by the other Mac over the cable) is implemented elsewhere and was not supplied. A reviewer of the code should confirm that the count is authenticated by the existing paired-link channel, so a local same-UID process or the cable peer cannot forge or replay it to cancel a setup. This is a denial-of-service concern only, within the existing owner-controlled cluster trust. The claim that `darkbloom stop` stops only the local Mac before the pair runs is also unverified. No finding is raised because no code was supplied to support one.
